output.headline: Premier League rivals step up calls to publish Manchester City verdict
output.standfirst:
• Rival Premier League clubs step up calls to publish Manchester City’s verdict

  • Ferran Soriano says City will fight the ruling after being found guilty on the vast majority of the Premier League’s 115 financial charges
output.bodyHtml:
Premier League clubs are pushing for the Manchester City verdict to be published as soon as possible, while the club digs in for a long battle to clear its name.

Manchester City’s chief executive, Ferran Soriano, told a meeting of the European Football Clubs board on Monday that the club will fight to prove its innocence after being found guilty by an independent commission of the vast majority of the Premier League’s 115 charges of breaching financial rules.

Related: Scale of City’s punishment is the only story but Premier League must bear some responsibility | Barney Ronay

Soriano’s willingness to address the guilty verdict against City, which first emerged on Friday but has yet to be confirmed publicly by the club or the Premier League, surprised other members of the EFC board, which includes two domestic rivals in Jean-Claude Blanc, the head of Ineos Sport and chief of international football relations at Manchester United, and the Everton owner, Dan Friedkin.

Soriano is understood to have addressed the board at the start of the meeting by requesting permission to make a brief statement. He said he disagreed with the ruling of the commission, and that he and City were confident of eventually winning their battle. He added that while it had been eight years since the allegations of financial misconduct were first made against City, a definitive conclusion to the saga could take considerably more time.

Other clubs remain frustrated by the ongoing delay, saying they are being kept in the dark over the details of the case and the likely timeframe for any resolution. Club executives received a broad outline of the independent commission’s findings against City last Thursday, but there has been no update since, and the verdict has yet to be published. One club source said on Monday: ‘All we have is a void, and it would be better for everyone if it was filled as soon as possible.’

Soriano declined to comment when approached by reporters after the EFC board meeting.

The Premier League has not commented, nor given any indication of when the judgment will be published.
output.progress: Rival clubs are pressing the Premier League to publish the verdict quickly, while Ferran Soriano insists Manchester City will contest it in full.
